mainTopic: Who may receive מעשר ראשון, the comparison of מעשר to תרומה, and why the משנה says an engaged בת לוי or בת כהן 'may not eat' מעשר.
overview: This amud opens with a ברייתא. רבי מאיר says מעשר ראשון goes to a לוי, and רבי אלעזר בן עזריה says it may also be given to a כהן. The גמרא learns רבי מאיר's view from a פסוק that calls מעשר 'תרומה', so like תרומה it is forbidden to a זר. The death penalty and the extra fifth stay limited to תרומה. The רבנן use the same comparison to teach that missing מעשר ראשון makes produce טבל. That comparison adds a death penalty beyond the plain לאו learned from רבי יוסי's ברייתא. The גמרא then asks why the משנה says an engaged בת לוי or בת כהן may not eat מעשר, since she is not a זר. רב ששת answers that she cannot authorize separating תרומת מעשר, and a ברייתא shows that a married woman can. מר בריה דרבנא answers instead that she gets no share of מעשר at the threshing floor, because of a general גזירה. The amud ends as a new ברייתא begins, with רבי עקיבא's view and the start of רבי אלעזר בן עזריה's reply, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Two views on who gets מעשר ראשון
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר says תרומה goes to a כהן and מעשר ראשון goes to a לוי. רבי אלעזר בן עזריה says a כהן may also have it.
steps.simpleTranslation: תרומה is for a כהן and the first tithe is for a לוי, says רבי מאיר. רבי אלעזר בן עזריה permits it to a כהן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא with two views on who may receive מעשר ראשון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר keeps the two gifts separate: תרומה goes to the כהן and מעשר goes to the לוי. רבי אלעזר בן עזריה lets a כהן receive מעשר too, since a כהן also comes from the tribe of לוי.

keyTerms.meaning: The first gift taken from produce and given to a כהן
The first tithe, a tenth of the produce, given to a לוי
He permits it

phrases.english: Teruma is for a kohen,
and the first tithe is for a Levite,
these are the words of Rabbi Meir.
Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya
permits it to a kohen.
phrases.notes: "It" means the first tithe.

steps.triggerLanguage: תְּרוּמָה לְכֹהֵן, וּמַעֲשֵׂר רִאשׁוֹן לְלֵוִי, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי מֵאִיר
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי מאיר: מעשר ראשון is for a לוי. רבי אלעזר בן עזריה: a כהן may also take it.

steps.title: Why would anyone forbid it to a כהן
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא is surprised by the word 'permits'. It seems to imply that someone forbids מעשר to a כהן.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Permits it'?! That implies there is someone who forbids it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the wording 'permits', because no one would forbid a כהן from eating מעשר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A כהן is also from the tribe of לוי, so he is not an outsider to מעשר. Saying רבי אלעזר בן עזריה 'permits' it suggests that רבי מאיר forbids it, and that makes no sense.

keyTerms.meaning: By implication
Someone who forbids

phrases.english: "Permits it"?!
Does that imply there is someone who forbids it?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתִּירוֹ?! מִכְּלָל דְּאִיכָּא מַאן דְּאָסַר
steps.kashyaTarget: The word 'מתירו' in רבי אלעזר בן עזריה's statement
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: 'Permits' implies that someone forbids it, but no one would forbid מעשר to a כהן, who is himself from the tribe of לוי.

steps.title: Read it as: one may give it even to a כהן
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא changes the wording. רבי אלעזר בן עזריה means a person may hand the מעשר to a כהן instead of a לוי.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, say: one gives it even to a כהן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by restating רבי אלעזר בן עזריה's words in a clearer way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The argument is not about whether a כהן may eat מעשר. It is about whether the owner may choose to give it to a כהן. רבי מאיר says it must go to a לוי. רבי אלעזר בן עזריה says a כהן is also a valid choice.

keyTerms.meaning: Say (read it this way)
He gives it
Even, also

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רבי מאיר forbids a כהן to eat מעשר. The argument is only about whom the owner gives it to.

phrases.english: Rather, say:
one gives it even to a kohen.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אֵימָא: נוֹתְנוֹ אַף לְכֹהֵן
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the wording of the ברייתא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי אלעזר בן עזריה permits eating, which implies that רבי מאיר forbids it.
steps.terutzMaskana: The argument is about giving: may the owner give מעשר to a כהן?

steps.title: What is רבי מאיר's reason
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source of רבי מאיר's view.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is רבי מאיר's reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why רבי מאיר holds this view. This sets up the source that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא wants a source showing that רבי מאיר treats מעשר ראשון as forbidden to outsiders, meaning non-לויים, the way תרומה is forbidden to non-כהנים.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason?

phrases.english: What is the reason of Rabbi Meir?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי מֵאִיר
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source for רבי מאיר's view that מעשר ראשון is for a לוי

steps.title: The פסוק calls מעשר 'תרומה'
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בריה דרבה quotes a פסוק that calls מעשר 'תרומה'. So, like תרומה, מעשר ראשון is forbidden to a זר.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא son of רבה said in the name of tradition: 'For the tithe of בני ישראל which they set apart to ה׳ as a תרומה.' Just as תרומה is forbidden to outsiders, so is מעשר ראשון forbidden to outsiders.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives רבי מאיר's source. A פסוק links מעשר to תרומה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah calls מעשר 'תרומה', so the two are compared. Just as a זר may not eat תרומה, a non-לוי may not eat מעשר ראשון. That is why רבי מאיר says it must go to a לוי.

keyTerms.meaning: In the name of received tradition
Outsiders, people not entitled to the gift
Just as ... so too (a comparison)

phrases.english: Rav Acha son of Rabba said
in the name of tradition:
"For the tithe of the children of Israel
which they set apart to ה׳ as a teruma."
phrases.notes: במדבר 18:24

phrases.english: Just as teruma is forbidden to outsiders,
so too the first tithe is forbidden to outsiders.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אַחָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַבָּה מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דִּגְמָרָא
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק calls מעשר 'תרומה', so like תרומה it is forbidden to a זר (a non-לוי).

steps.title: Should מעשר also carry death and the extra fifth
steps.stepSummary: If מעשר is fully like תרומה, a זר who eats it should get death from Heaven and pay an extra fifth.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, just as for תרומה one is liable to death and the extra fifth, should one also be liable to death and the extra fifth for מעשר?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the comparison. If it is complete, all the strict rules of תרומה should apply to מעשר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A זר who eats תרומה is punished with death from Heaven and must pay its value plus a fifth. The comparison seems to force the same rules onto מעשר, and that is a big step.

keyTerms.meaning: Death from Heaven
The extra fifth added when paying back
If (so)

phrases.english: If so, just as with teruma
one is liable for it to death and a fifth,
so too with tithe,
should one be liable for it to death and a fifth?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי מָה תְּרוּמָה חַיָּיבִין עָלָיו מִיתָה וָחוֹמֶשׁ
steps.kashyaTarget: The comparison of מעשר to תרומה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A full comparison would bring the death penalty and the extra fifth to מעשר too.

steps.title: The פסוקים limit death and the fifth to תרומה
steps.stepSummary: The words 'בו' and 'עליו' teach that death and the extra fifth apply only to תרומה, not to מעשר.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: 'They will die through it if they profane it' and 'He shall add its fifth to it.' 'Through it' and not through מעשר; 'to it' and not to מעשר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the Torah itself limits the harsh punishments to תרומה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'בו' (through it) and 'עליו' (to it) point only to תרומה and leave out מעשר. So the comparison keeps the ban on outsiders, but the punishments do not carry over.

keyTerms.meaning: The פסוק says
They profane it
Its fifth

phrases.english: The verse says:
"And they will die through it if they profane it,"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 22:9

phrases.english: "And he shall add its fifth to it."
phrases.notes: ויקרא 22:14

phrases.english: "Through it" and not through tithe;
"to it" and not to tithe.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר קְרָא: וּמֵתוּ בוֹ כִּי יְחַלְּלֻהוּ
steps.terutzHavaAmina: מעשר would carry death and the extra fifth just like תרומה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ban on outsiders carries over, but death and the extra fifth are only for תרומה.
steps.whatToRemember: For רבי מאיר, מעשר ראשון is forbidden to a non-לוי because the Torah calls it 'תרומה', but there is no death penalty or extra fifth.

steps.title: The רבנן learn טבל from the comparison
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן do not use the comparison to forbid מעשר to outsiders. They learn that מעשר ראשון, like תרומה, makes produce into טבל.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the רבנן? Just as תרומה makes produce טבל, so too מעשר ראשון makes produce טבל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what the רבנן learn from the פסוק that calls מעשר 'תרומה', and answers in the same breath.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן disagree with רבי מאיר, but they still need the comparison to teach something. For them it teaches that produce from which מעשר ראשון has not yet been taken is טבל and may not be eaten, just as with תרומה.

keyTerms.meaning: The Sages who disagree with רבי מאיר
Makes produce into טבל (forbidden until the gifts are taken)
Also

steps.confusionAlert: 'טובלת' here has nothing to do with immersing. It means 'makes the produce טבל', forbidden until the gift is separated.

phrases.english: And the Rabbis?
phrases.notes: He's asking: what do the רבנן learn from this פסוק?

phrases.english: Just as teruma makes produce tevel,
so too the first tithe also makes it tevel.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבָּנַן, מָה תְּרוּמָה טוֹבֶלֶת
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The רבנן use the comparison to teach that מעשר ראשון makes produce into טבל, just like תרומה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that both sides accept the comparison between מעשר and תרומה. They only argue about what it teaches.

steps.title: רבי יוסי: produce stays טבל until every gift is taken
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא of רבי יוסי begins to ask where we learn that produce is still טבל when only some of the gifts have been taken.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is taught: רבי יוסי says, one might think a person is liable only for טבל from which nothing at all was taken. If תרומה גדולה was taken but not מעשר ראשון, or מעשר ראשון but not מעשר שני, or even only מעשר עני is missing, from where do we learn it is still טבל?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to back up the רבנן's teaching that מעשר also makes produce טבל. Step 10 gives the answer to רבי יוסי's question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי asks whether produce counts as טבל only when nothing was taken. He wants a source that missing מעשר ראשון, מעשר שני, or even מעשר עני still keeps it טבל. This matches the רבנן's reading that טבל status is not limited to תרומה.

keyTerms.meaning: And as it is taught in a ברייתא
One might have thought
Produce from which the required gifts were not yet taken
Was separated, set apart
The tithe for the poor
From where do we know?

phrases.english: And as it is taught:
Rabbi Yosei says:
One might think a person is not liable
except for tevel
from which nothing at all was separated.
If the great teruma was separated from it
but the first tithe was not separated from it;
or the first tithe but not the second tithe;
and even the poor man's tithe,
phrases.notes: Meaning: even if only the poor man's tithe is still missing.

phrases.english: from where do we know?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִדְתַנְיָא, רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר
steps.raayaObject: The רבנן's teaching that מעשר ראשון makes produce into טבל
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא of רבי יוסי about produce from which only some of the gifts were taken

steps.title: רבי יוסי links two verses through the word 'your gates'
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי proves from the word 'שעריך' that produce stays forbidden even when only מעשר עני has not been taken.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse says: 'You may not eat within your gates.' Later it says: 'They will eat within your gates and be satisfied.' The second verse is about מעשר עני, so the first verse is also about מעשר עני. The Torah says 'you may not' eat, so the food is forbidden until מעשר עני is taken.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the ברייתא of רבי יוסי from step 9. It shows the source that food is still טבל even when only one gift is missing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same word 'שעריך' appears in both פסוקים, so we read them together. The second פסוק is about מעשר עני, so the first פסוק, which says 'you may not eat', is also about a case where only מעשר עני is missing. That means even one missing gift keeps the produce forbidden as טבל.

keyTerms.meaning: The verse teaches. This introduces the source from a פסוק.
Your gates, meaning your towns. This is the linking word between the two פסוקים.
The tithe given to the poor in certain years.
The Merciful One, a name for ה׳ as the Giver of the Torah.
Below or elsewhere. It refers to the other פסוק being compared.

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source that every single gift, not only תרומה, keeps produce in the forbidden status of טבל.

phrases.english: The verse states: "You may not eat within your gates,"
phrases.notes: דברים 12:17

phrases.english: and below it states:
"That they may eat within your gates and be satisfied."
phrases.notes: דברים 26:12. That פסוק is about giving מעשר עני to the poor.

phrases.english: Just as "your gates" stated below
is the poor man's tithe,
so too "your gates" stated here
is the poor man's tithe,
and the Merciful One said "you may not" eat.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: לֹא תוּכַל לֶאֱכוֹל בִּשְׁעָרֶיךָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the ברייתא of רבי יוסי that step 9 began.
steps.raayaObject: That produce remains טבל even when only some of the gifts, such as מעשר עני, have not been separated.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The shared word 'שעריך' in דברים 12:17 and דברים 26:12.

steps.title: Why the comparison to תרומה is still needed: it adds the death penalty
steps.stepSummary: From רבי יוסי alone we would know only a plain prohibition. The comparison to תרומה teaches that eating this טבל brings death from Heaven.
steps.simpleTranslation: If we only had רבי יוסי's source, I would think it is just a regular prohibition, with no death penalty. So the comparison to תרומה teaches us that there is a death penalty.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers an unspoken question. If רבי יוסי already teaches that מעשר makes food טבל, why do the רבנן need the comparison to תרומה from step 8?
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי's verse says only 'you may not eat', which sounds like a plain לאו. The comparison to תרומה adds the stronger punishment of מיתה בידי שמים for eating this טבל. So each source teaches something different.

keyTerms.meaning: I would have thought. This is the mistaken first idea.
A plain negative commandment, without the death penalty.
Death, here meaning death from Heaven.
It teaches us. This brings the new point.

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix this up with step 7. There, 'בו' and 'עליו' teach that a זר eating מעשר gets no death penalty. Here the death penalty is for eating טבל, food from which the gifts were never taken.

phrases.english: And if we learned it only from there,
phrases.notes: From there means from רבי יוסי's verse.

phrases.english: I would have said it is only a prohibition,
but the death penalty, no;
so it teaches us.
phrases.notes: It means the comparison of מעשר to תרומה, which shows there is a death penalty.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי מֵהָתָם, הֲוָה אָמֵינָא לְלָאו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains why the רבנן's source in step 8 is not made unnecessary by רבי יוסי in step 10.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Each source teaches something different: a plain prohibition versus the death penalty.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Eating טבל of מעשר is only a plain לאו.
steps.terutzMaskana: The comparison to תרומה teaches that it carries מיתה בידי שמים.

steps.title: Another version: we already know this from רבי יוסי
steps.stepSummary: In the other version, the גמרא openly asks why we need the comparison, since רבי יוסי already teaches that מעשר ראשון makes food טבל.
steps.simpleTranslation: A different version: The rule that מעשר ראשון makes food טבל comes from רבי יוסי! So why do we need the comparison to תרומה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second way the discussion was told. Here the question is asked out loud as a challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 11 answered a question the גמרא never said out loud. This version says the question openly: רבי יוסי already gives the source, so the רבנן's comparison looks unnecessary. The answer comes in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: A different version of the same discussion.
It makes the food טבל, forbidden until the gifts are taken.
It comes out from, meaning it is learned from.

phrases.english: A different version:
that the first tithe creates the status of untithed produce,
that is derived from Rabbi Yosei!

steps.triggerLanguage: לִישָּׁנָא אַחֲרִינָא: מַעֲשֵׂר רִאשׁוֹן דְּטָבֵיל, מִדְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי נָפְקָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Retells step 11 in a second version. The question step 11 left unspoken (why the comparison is needed if רבי יוסי in steps 9–10 already teaches it) is now asked openly as a challenge.
steps.kashyaTarget: The רבנן's use of the comparison of מעשר to תרומה to teach that מעשר makes food טבל (step 8).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יוסי's verse already teaches this, so the comparison seems unnecessary.

steps.title: The answer in the other version: the death penalty
steps.stepSummary: From רבי יוסי alone we would know only a לאו. The comparison teaches the death penalty.
steps.simpleTranslation: If we had only that source, I would say it is just a prohibition, with no death penalty. So it teaches us that there is a death penalty.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge of step 12 with the same answer as step 11.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two versions reach the same point. רבי יוסי gives only a לאו, and the comparison to תרומה adds מיתה. The only difference is whether the question was said out loud.

keyTerms.meaning: From that one, meaning רבי יוסי's source.

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוסי teaches that any missing gift makes food forbidden as טבל. The comparison of מעשר to תרומה adds that eating such טבל brings death from Heaven.

phrases.english: If we learned it from that source alone,
I would have said it is only a prohibition,
but the death penalty, no;
so it teaches us.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי מֵהַהִיא, הֲוָה אָמֵינָא לְלָאו
steps.terutzResolutionType: Each source teaches something different: a plain prohibition versus the death penalty.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Without the comparison, eating טבל of מעשר would be only a לאו.
steps.terutzMaskana: The comparison adds מיתה בידי שמים.

steps.title: The end of the משנה doesn't fit רבי מאיר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: if the משנה follows רבי מאיר, why can't a בת לוי engaged to a כהן, or a בת כהן engaged to a לוי, eat מעשר? She is not a זר.
steps.simpleTranslation: How did you explain the משנה? Like רבי מאיר. Then look at the end: a בת לוי engaged to a כהן, and a בת כהן engaged to a לוי, may eat neither תרומה nor מעשר. Here, what outsider status is there?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the משנה and attacks the earlier explanation that it follows רבי מאיר, who forbids מעשר to a זר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the משנה forbids מעשר only because of רבי מאיר's rule against a זר eating it, these women should be allowed to eat. A בת לוי or בת כהן is not a זר for מעשר at all. So why does the משנה say she may not eat it?

keyTerms.meaning: How did you explain it? This asks which opinion the משנה follows.
Say the end part of the משנה.
Engaged, after אירוסין but before נישואין.
Being an outsider, a זר, for these holy gifts.

phrases.english: How did you establish the mishna? In accordance with Rabbi Meir.
phrases.notes: Earlier the גמרא explained the משנה like רבי מאיר, who says a זר may not eat מעשר ראשון.

phrases.english: Then say the latter clause:
The daughter of a Levite betrothed to a priest,
and the daughter of a priest betrothed to a Levite,

phrases.aramaic: לֹא תֹּאכַל לֹא בִּתְרוּמָה וְלֹא בְּמַעֲשֵׂר,
phrases.english: may eat neither teruma nor tithe.
Here, what foreignness is there?
phrases.notes: Either way she comes from a family of לויים or כהנים, so she is not an outsider for מעשר.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּמַאי אוֹקֵימְתַּהּ — כְּרַבִּי מֵאִיר, אֵימָא סֵיפָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the source discussion and returns to the משנה, testing the claim that it follows רבי מאיר.
steps.kashyaTarget: The explanation that the משנה follows רבי מאיר, who forbids מעשר ראשון to a זר.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In the end part of the משנה, the woman is not a זר, yet she is still forbidden to eat מעשר. So 'not eating' cannot be about זרות.

steps.title: רב ששת: 'she may not eat' means she may not give permission to separate
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת explains that in this case 'אינה אוכלת' means she cannot authorize separating תרומת מעשר from her fiancé's מעשר.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת said: What does the משנה mean by 'she may not eat'? It means she may not give permission to separate תרומה from the מעשר.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת answers the challenge by reading the משנה's words in a different way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since she is only engaged, she is not yet his wife. So she cannot let others separate תרומת מעשר from his מעשר on his behalf. The משנה's words 'she may not eat' are not about eating at all, so the question about זרות falls away.

keyTerms.meaning: Permission or authority to act for someone.
To separate תרומה, here the תרומה taken from the מעשר.

steps.confusionAlert: Here 'אינה אוכלת' does not mean she can't eat. רב ששת reads it as 'she has no authority to separate' from her fiancé's מעשר.
steps.whatToRemember: The משנה still fits רבי מאיר. In the end part, 'she may not eat' means she may not give permission to separate, because an engaged woman is not yet her husband's wife.

phrases.english: Rav Sheshet said:
What does "she may not eat," which the mishna teaches, mean?
She may not give permission to separate teruma.
phrases.notes: She is only engaged, so she can't let others take תרומת מעשר from her fiancé's מעשר for him.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב שֵׁשֶׁת: מַאי אֵינָהּ אוֹכֶלֶת דְּקָתָנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 14 by reading the משנה's words differently.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting the wording of the משנה.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'אינה אוכלת' means she may not eat the מעשר, which would make no sense since she is not a זר.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'אינה אוכלת' means she cannot authorize separating תרומת מעשר, because an engaged woman is not yet a wife.

steps.title: Does this mean a married woman can authorize separation?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether רב ששת's answer implies that a married woman may authorize separating תרומת מעשר.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does this imply that a married woman can give permission to separate?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws an inference from רב ששת's answer and checks whether it is true. This sets up the proof that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב ששת said an engaged woman cannot authorize separating תרומת מעשר from her fiancé's מעשר. That suggests a fully married woman can. The גמרא asks whether that is really the הלכה.

keyTerms.meaning: By implication; we can infer
A fully married woman (after the wedding)
Gives permission (to someone else to separate)

phrases.english: Does this imply that a married woman gives permission?
phrases.notes: He means permission to separate תרומת מעשר from her husband's מעשר, the opposite of the engaged woman in step 15.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִכְלָל דִּנְשׂוּאָה נוֹתֶנֶת רְשׁוּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws an inference from רב ששת's answer.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is it true that a married woman may authorize separating תרומת מעשר from her husband's מעשר?

steps.title: Yes, a ברייתא teaches it from a פסוק
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers yes and quotes a ברייתא: the פסוק 'you and your households' teaches that a בת ישראל married to a לוי may authorize separation.
steps.simpleTranslation: Yes. A ברייתא teaches: 'And you may eat it in any place, you and your households.' This teaches that a married בת ישראל may give permission to separate.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא confirms the inference and backs it up with a ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא reads 'your households' in the פסוק about מעשר as including the לוי's wife. From this it learns that a בת ישראל married to a לוי has authority to have תרומת מעשר separated from his מעשר.

keyTerms.meaning: Yes
And it was taught in a ברייתא
To separate (תרומה or תרומת מעשר)

phrases.english: Yes, and it was taught:
"And you may eat it in any place,
phrases.notes: במדבר 18:31, a פסוק about the לוי's מעשר.

phrases.english: you and your households" —
it teaches about a married בת ישראל
phrases.notes: She is married to a לוי, so 'your households' includes her.

phrases.english: that she gives permission to separate.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִין, וְהָתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 16 with a ברייתא.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Yes; the ברייתא learns from 'you and your households' that a married בת ישראל may authorize separating תרומת מעשר.

steps.title: Maybe the פסוק is only about eating?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks itself: perhaps the פסוק teaches that she may eat מעשר, not that she may authorize separation.
steps.simpleTranslation: Do you say it means permission to separate, or perhaps it only means permission to eat?
steps.whatsHappening: Still inside the ברייתא, a challenge is raised to its own reading of the פסוק. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The plain words of the פסוק talk about eating. So it seems the simplest reading is that the לוי's wife may eat מעשר, not that she has power to separate.

keyTerms.meaning: Do you say (introduces a challenge to a reading)
Or perhaps it is only
To eat

phrases.english: You say permission to separate,
or is it only to eat?

steps.triggerLanguage: אַתָּה אוֹמֵר רְשׁוּת לִתְרוֹם, אוֹ אֵינוֹ אֶלָּא לֶאֱכוֹל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The ברייתא challenges its own reading of the פסוק.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's reading that the פסוק is about authority to separate.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק literally says 'eat', so it should teach permission to eat, not to separate.

steps.title: Eating is already known by a קל וחומר
steps.stepSummary: Eating needs no פסוק: if a בת ישראל married to a כהן eats strict תרומה, surely she eats lenient מעשר. So the פסוק must teach permission to separate.
steps.simpleTranslation: You can say: if she eats strict תרומה, surely she eats lenient מעשר! Rather, it teaches that a married בת ישראל may give permission to separate.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers its own challenge with a קל וחומר and goes back to its first reading.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A בת ישראל married to a כהן may eat תרומה, which is stricter than מעשר. So a בת ישראל married to a לוי can surely eat מעשר, and the פסוק is not needed for that. Since the פסוק must teach something new, it teaches that she may authorize separation.

keyTerms.meaning: Strict, more serious
The lenient one
Surely all the more so (a קל וחומר)

steps.whatToRemember: A woman married to a לוי can authorize separating תרומת מעשר from his מעשר. This comes from 'you and your households', because eating is already known from a קל וחומר.

phrases.english: You can say: she eats תרומה, which is strict,
phrases.notes: This is about a בת ישראל married to a כהן.

phrases.english: so surely she eats מעשר, which is lenient?!

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא לִימֵּד עַל נְשׂוּאָה בַּת יִשְׂרָאֵל
phrases.english: Rather, it teaches about a married בת ישראל
that she gives permission to separate.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרַתְּ: תְּרוּמָה חֲמוּרָה אוֹכֶלֶת, מַעֲשֵׂר הַקַּל לֹא כׇּל שֶׁכֵּן
steps.terutzResolutionType: קל וחומר shows the 'eating' reading is unnecessary, so the פסוק teaches separation.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פסוק teaches that the לוי's wife may eat מעשר.
steps.terutzMaskana: Eating is known from a קל וחומר from תרומה; the פסוק teaches that she may authorize separation.

steps.title: Another answer: she is not given מעשר at the threshing floor
steps.stepSummary: מר בריה דרבנא answers the question of step 14 differently: 'she does not eat' means she is not given a share of מעשר at the threshing floor.
steps.simpleTranslation: מר בריה דרבנא said: it means that we do not give her a share of מעשר at the threshing floors.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the question of step 14 and gives a second answer, different from רב ששת's.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question was why the engaged woman 'cannot eat' מעשר when she is not a זר. מר בריה דרבנא says she may eat it, but the משנה means that the מעשר is not handed out to her at the threshing floor.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא, מר the son of רבנא
Distribute, give out shares
The threshing floors, where produce is distributed

phrases.english: מר בריה דרבנא said:
It comes to say that we do not distribute to her
מעשר at the threshing floors.

steps.triggerLanguage: מָר בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַבְנָא אָמַר: לוֹמַר שֶׁאֵין חוֹלְקִין לָהּ מַעֲשֵׂר בְּבֵית הַגְּרָנוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second answer to step 14, alongside רב ששת's answer in step 15.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterprets 'אינה אוכלת' as not receiving a share at the threshing floor.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה forbids her to eat מעשר even though she is not a זר.
steps.terutzMaskana: She may eat, but she is not given מעשר at the threshing floor.

steps.title: This fits only one reason for the threshing-floor rule
steps.stepSummary: The answer works if women are kept from the threshing floor because of ייחוד, but not if the reason is fear she is divorced, since a divorced בת לוי still eats מעשר.
steps.simpleTranslation: This works for the one who says the reason is ייחוד. But for the one who says it is because she may be divorced: does a divorced בת לוי not eat מעשר?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges מר בריה דרבנא's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two reasons given for not handing out shares to women at the threshing floor: ייחוד, or fear that she is secretly divorced and no longer allowed. The ייחוד reason applies here too. But a divorced בת לוי still eats מעשר in her own right, so the divorce worry does not apply to her.

keyTerms.meaning: This works for the one who says
Being alone with a man who is not her husband
A divorced woman

phrases.english: This works for the one who says it is because of ייחוד,
phrases.notes: There is a known rule that women are not given shares at the threshing floor; two reasons are given for it.

phrases.english: but for the one who says it is because of a divorcée,
a divorced בת לוי,
does she not eat מעשר?!

steps.triggerLanguage: הָנִיחָא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר מִשּׁוּם יִיחוּד, אֶלָּא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר מִשּׁוּם גְּרוּשָׁה
steps.kashyaTarget: מר בריה דרבנא's claim that the בת לוי is not given מעשר at the threshing floor.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the rule exists because she may be divorced, it should not apply to a בת לוי, who eats מעשר even when divorced.

steps.title: It is a blanket גזירה because of a divorced בת ישראל
steps.stepSummary: The same problem exists with a divorced בת כהן, who still eats תרומה. So the rule must be a general גזירה made because of a divorced בת ישראל.
steps.simpleTranslation: And by your reasoning, does a divorced בת כהן not eat תרומה? Rather, it is a גזירה because of a divorced בת ישראל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns the question back on the asker and answers by explaining that the rule is a general גזירה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even a divorced בת כהן still eats תרומה, yet women are not given תרומה at the threshing floor. So the rule is not about each woman's own status. It is a blanket גזירה made because of a divorced בת ישראל, who really loses the right, and it covers everyone, including the בת לוי.

keyTerms.meaning: And according to your reasoning
A rabbinic decree made as a safeguard
Daughter of a כהן

steps.whatToRemember: The threshing-floor rule is a blanket גזירה because of a divorced בת ישראל. So it applies even to women who could eat on their own, which supports מר בריה דרבנא.

phrases.english: And by your reasoning, a divorced בת כהן,
does she not eat תרומה?
phrases.notes: Yet she still isn't given תרומה at the threshing floor, so the same question would hit her.

phrases.english: Rather, it is a decree
because of a divorced בת ישראל.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלִיטַעְמָיךְ, גְּרוּשָׁה בַּת כֹּהֵן מִי לָא אָכְלָה בִּתְרוּמָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 21 and defends מר בריה דרבנא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Counter-question showing the rule is a blanket decree, not based on each woman's own status.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The divorce reason applies only to women who would lose the right after divorce.
steps.terutzMaskana: The rule is a general גזירה because of a divorced בת ישראל, covering even a בת כהן or בת לוי.

steps.title: Why only a betrothed woman?
steps.stepSummary: If she gets no share of מעשר at the threshing floor because of a general גזירה, that should be true for a married woman too. So why does the משנה mention only a מאורסת?
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, why does the משנה speak specifically of a betrothed woman? The same rule should apply even to a married woman!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer from step 20. If that answer is correct, why does the משנה limit the rule to a betrothed woman?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under מר בריה דרבנא, 'she does not eat' means she gets no share at the threshing floor. That is because of the general גזירה about a divorced woman. That concern has nothing to do with being betrothed rather than married. A married בת לוי is kept away from the threshing floor just the same, so the word מאורסת seems to add nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: If so; if your explanation is correct
Why specifically this case?
A betrothed woman (after קידושין, before נישואין)
A fully married woman

phrases.english: If so,
phrases.notes: Meaning: if the reason is the threshing-floor גזירה from steps 20–22.

phrases.english: why specifically a betrothed woman?
Even a married woman as well!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי, מַאי אִירְיָא מְאוֹרֶסֶת? אֲפִילּוּ נְשׂוּאָה נָמֵי!
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts the גזירה from step 22, then asks why the משנה's wording is so narrow
steps.kashyaTarget: The word מאורסת in the משנה, as read by מר בריה דרבנא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The reason given (a general threshing-floor גזירה) applies equally to a married woman, so limiting the case to a betrothed woman seems pointless

steps.title: The second part copies the wording of the first
steps.stepSummary: The first part of the משנה spoke of a betrothed woman, so the second part used the same word, even though its rule applies to a married woman too.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since the first part of the משנה taught 'betrothed,' it also taught 'betrothed' in the second part.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the word 'betrothed' in the second part has no special meaning. It just matches the wording of the first part.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This answer is about style, not law. The תנא kept both parts of the משנה parallel. So the rule in the second part truly applies to a married woman as well, and מר בריה דרבנא's explanation stands.

keyTerms.meaning: Since he taught (this wording elsewhere)
The first part of a משנה or ברייתא
The later part of a משנה or ברייתא

steps.confusionAlert: Do not conclude that a married בת לוי is treated differently. The word 'betrothed' here is only matching wording; the rule covers her too.

phrases.english: Since he taught 'betrothed' in the first part,
he also taught 'betrothed' in the later part.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַיְּידֵי דִּתְנָא רֵישָׁא מְאוֹרֶסֶת, תְּנָא נָמֵי סֵיפָא מְאוֹרֶסֶת
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The word מאורסת must limit the law to a betrothed woman
steps.terutzMaskana: The word only mirrors the first part. The law applies to a married woman too.
steps.whatToRemember: מר בריה דרבנא's reading survives. 'She does not eat מעשר' means she gets no share at the threshing floor, because of a general גזירה. The word 'betrothed' in that part of the משנה just repeats the wording of the first part.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא: מעשר ראשון goes only to a לוי
steps.stepSummary: A new ברייתא opens. רבי עקיבא holds that תרומה goes to a כהן and מעשר ראשון goes to a לוי. רבי אלעזר בן עזריה begins to give a different view.
steps.simpleTranslation: The rabbis taught: תרומה goes to a כהן, and מעשר ראשון goes to a לוי. These are the words of רבי עקיבא. רבי אלעזר בן עזריה says:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא about who may receive מעשר ראשון. The amud ends just as רבי אלעזר בן עזריה starts to speak, so his opinion comes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא keeps each gift with its own group: תרומה for a כהן, מעשר ראשון for a לוי. That suggests a כהן does not take מעשר ראשון. The setup with 'רבי אלעזר בן עזריה says' signals a dispute about that point.

keyTerms.meaning: The rabbis taught (introduces a ברייתא)
The gift of produce given to a כהן
The first tithe, given to a לוי
The words of; the opinion of

phrases.english: The rabbis taught:
תרומה goes to a כהן,
and the first tithe goes to a לוי,
these are the words of רבי עקיבא.
רבי אלעזר בן עזריה says:
phrases.notes: His actual opinion comes at the start of the next amud.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: תְּרוּמָה לְכֹהֵן, וּמַעֲשֵׂר רִאשׁוֹן לְלֵוִי, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the משנה's case and opens a new ברייתא about who receives מעשר ראשון
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי עקיבא: תרומה goes to a כהן, and מעשר ראשון goes to a לוי. רבי אלעזר בן עזריה's opposing view comes next.
steps.whyThisMatters: This ברייתא sets up a dispute about whether a כהן may also receive מעשר ראשון. That question connects to the earlier talk of who eats מעשר.
